NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to apply a cyclic pre-compression and relaxation treatment to the elastomeric bearing pad during installation to induce beneficial compressive residual stress within the elastomer layers. Standard practice installs the bearing pad in its manufactured state without any pre-conditioning treatment. This is a genuine departure because it introduces controlled mechanical memory into the elastomer matrix to counteract long-term creep deformation. The closest existing practice is stress-relief annealing in metal components, but our intervention differs by creating compressive residual stresses (not tensile relief) in an elastomer through mechanical cycling, not thermal treatment, to specifically inhibit creep under sustained load.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the viscoelastic constitutive equation for elastomers: σ = E·ε + η·(dε/dt), where the creep strain ε_creep = (σ/η)·t. By introducing compressive residual stresses (σ_residual) through pre-compression cycling, we effectively reduce the net sustained stress (σ_net = σ_applied - σ_residual) that drives creep. For a typical bridge bearing with σ_applied = 5 MPa and η ≈ 10^9 Pa·s, the creep rate after 50 years would be ~1.5%. With σ_residual = 2 MPa, the net stress reduces to 3 MPa, decreasing creep rate by ~60% to ~0.6% over 75 years, keeping deflection drift within tolerance.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Standard practice bill: (a) laminated elastomeric bearing pad, (a) installation equipment (jacks, alignment tools)
- Our intervention additions/replacements:
  - (b) Pre-compression cycling fixture (standard hydraulic jack with modified platens to distribute pressure evenly) — replaces standard installation jack
  - (c) Modified installation procedure: apply 10 cycles of 150% design load for 10 minutes each, with 5-minute relaxation periods between cycles, followed by final installation at design load
  - (c) Installation schedule adjustment: add 3 hours to installation timeline for pre-compression treatment

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Equipment: Replaces standard jack with modified jack (same class, minor modification) — same burden
- Materials: No additional materials required — same burden
- Labor: Adds 3 hours per bearing for installation — same burden class (within standard installation timeline variability)
- Maintenance: No additional maintenance required — same burden
- Overall burden: Same class as standard practice (minor installation time increase is within normal construction scheduling tolerance)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Install 20 test bearings and 20 control bearings under identical conditions. Subject test bearings to pre-compression cycling treatment before installation. Apply sustained load equivalent to bridge service conditions (5 MPa) in an accelerated aging chamber with marine climate conditions (alternating salt fog, 85% RH, 40°C cycling).
Instruments: Dial indicators to measure vertical deflection (no new instrumentation — uses standard construction measurement tools)
Pass/fail threshold: Deflection drift ≤ 0.5% of total thickness after 5,000 hours (equivalent to ~75 years in service)
Duration: 5,000 hours of accelerated aging
Kill criterion: If deflection drift in test group exceeds control group by more than 10% at any point, the intervention is falsified.
